entry.title: Softfork before GTA VI?
entry.summary:
Soft fork development is a complex and non-linear process, often shaped by the discovery of real vulnerabilities that demand immediate attention. For instance, work on APO in 2022 revealed the "Replacement Cycling Attack" while reviewing its integration into Lightning channels. This vulnerability was significant enough to prompt discussions about whether a soft fork would be required for a proper fix. The disclosure of this issue led to public debate, and the existence of such a vulnerability had a discouraging effect, slowing down or even halting progress on APO. Despite substantial effort, resources, and dedication invested in advancing soft-fork changes, there remains an inherent uncertainty; unforeseen technical obstacles can emerge at any stage, prioritizing the resolution of severe security issues over continued development.
Participation in the review and implementation process of proposals like BIP54 is open to everyone globally. Community members are encouraged to contribute by reviewing the BIP, engaging with its implementations—such as the ongoing pull request in Bitcoin Core ([https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35793](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35793))—or assisting with quality assurance efforts to enhance its standards. Even those lacking deep analytical skills or specialized knowledge can add value through community engagement, as discussed in forums such as [this Google Groups thread](https://groups.google.com/g/bitcoindev/c/TBBakeBK8_E) and through participation in related discussions ([https://github.com/bitschmidty/bip54/issues/15](https://github.com/bitschmidty/bip54/issues/15)). The ethos encourages individuals not to passively await advancements from the developer community but to actively seek ways to contribute themselves to the progress they wish to see.
There is no direct evidence or personal experience suggesting that custodial services have attempted to obstruct the advancement of covenant-related developments. While it cannot be definitively ruled out, there have been no first-hand reports or recollections of such interference.
